question: How is backpropagation related to gradient descent?
direct_answer: Backpropagation computes the gradients; gradient descent uses those gradients to update the parameters.
expanded_answer: These are distinct steps with different roles. Backpropagation is an efficient algorithm for calculating partial derivatives of the loss with respect to each parameter in a neural network. Gradient descent is the optimization rule that uses those derivatives to adjust the parameters. So backpropagation supplies the information, and gradient descent performs the learning update.
key_points: Gradient descent applies the update rule
Backprop is not itself an optimizer
They are complementary parts of training
common_wrong_ideas: Backpropagation and gradient descent are the same algorithm
Gradient descent can work without gradients
